newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, bellies end higher on talk of light runs.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, bellies end higher on talk of light runs.

text.p: CME hogs and pork belly futures closed higher amid talk supplies of market-ready hogs are gradually declining, traders said.
Pork bellies closed higher, but traders said much of the buying appeared to be local shortcovering and not geared to a fundamental factors.
After the close, USDA estimated Thursday's hog slaughter at 370,000 head, which exceeded analysts' estimates.
The large slaughter coupled with steady to higher cash hog prices Thursday may be bullish for Friday's cash and futures hog markets, analysts said.
One analyst said cash hogs may trade $0.50 per cwt higher in Midwest markets Friday.
Some buying in hogs and pork belly futures was attributed to the market correcting after steep declines Wednesday which some analysts said were excessive.
Trading in pork bellies was light late in the session and largely featured light volume local trading.

Hogs closed up 0.575 to 0.175 cent, with December up 0.450 at 59.250 cents a lb and February lean hogs up 0.300 at 77.175 cents. Pork bellies closed up 1.200 to down 0.025 cent, with February up 0.750 at 78.600 cents.
